column1: # Token patterns for the Korean-naturalness reviewer, read by scripts/scan.py.
# One row per pattern. Tab-separated; lines starting with # are comments.
#   regex      Python re, run per line of prose with markup blanked;
#              prefix (?#raw) to run it on the line with markup kept
#   min_count  N: report only when one paragraph holds N hits (a blank-line block
#              in Markdown/text, one ko: value in YAML); file:N counts the whole file
#   example    a string the regex must match (checked by --check-lexicon)
#              optional, |-separated strings the regex must not match at all:
#              the natural Korean a narrowed regex was narrowed to leave alone
#              (checked by --check-lexicon; a row may leave the cell out)
# Hits are candidates: the reviewer confirms each by reading the line.
# Personal-corpus rows go in patterns.local.tsv, which overrides by id.

column7: why
Japanese-syntax (~において) residue; a locative `저장소에 있어서` (because it is in the repository) is a false positive.
Direct from English "to have X" with an abstract noun; Korean prefers a predicate.
English "It is" / "This is" rendered literally; Korean drops a subject the context already supplies.
column8: Drop the subject and restructure as `~이다`

column7: English passive translated literally; Korean prefers active voice unless the agent is unknown or irrelevant.
Three or more chained possessives read as a syntactic stack ("X's Y's Z's W").
column8: Restructure with a verb: `X가 운영하는 Y의 Z`

column6: API를 통해 배포하고 CLI를 통해 확인
column7: `통해/통해서` from English "through/via"; repeated within one paragraph it reads as a translation tic.

column6: 자동화함으로써 시간을 줄이고 표준화함으로써 실수를 막았다
column7: Direct from English "by doing X"; one per paragraph is fine, clustered use reads stilted.
Japanese-style nominalization plus `진행/수행/실시`; the noun is already a verb stem.
Causative `시키다` after `~화` is overformal; `~화하다` is the direct verb.
English "will" rendered literally in a plan or assertion; Korean states plans in the present or with `예정`.
Overly formal Japanese-Korean hybrid residue.
A plain English common noun left in Korean prose where a Korean word exists; distinct from product names and kept tech labels.
column8: `incident → 장애`, `silent failure → 감지되지 않는 장애`, `estate → 환경 / 인프라`

column7: Korean `압력` is physical pressure only, never I/O load or contention.
Korean `정렬` is lining up or sorting, never "make two configs agree"; a real sort is a false positive.
column9: 표 행을 재정렬한다|표 파이프와 정렬 행을 유지한다|이름 순으로 정렬하고|검색 결과를 기준으로 정렬한다

column7: Korean `수렴` is dominated by "gather opinions"; and you converge state, not drift.
Korean `재활용` carries a waste/garbage connotation and undercuts a "no extra investment" point.
Abstract nominalization that leaves no picture; the real act is writing it down so it does not recur.
Not a Korean word at all; a coinage for "indirection".
Korean `경로` is a physical route or file path; a hand-off is not a route.
Korean `함정` is a trap someone dug on purpose; nobody dug it, you hit it. A technical doc naming a known pitfall is a false positive; this row targets resume copy.
Marathon metaphor in operations prose, and it usually drags the object wrong (the upgrade, not the stack).
`주기를 설계·운영한다` does not hold; a cycle is not an operable object.
English stacks adjective+noun freely; Korean does not form this compound (controlled or controlling?).
You do not optimize noise; you reduce it.
Korean stacks 부채 / 피로 / 데이터, not `구조`.
English stem with the Korean `~화` suffix.
Empty abstract noun standing where a concrete one belongs; check the umbrella actually covers its own children.
column8: Name the real thing: `롤아웃이 멈추지 않습니다`, `클러스터 하나`, `인프라`

column7: `fail open` / `fail closed` rendered word for word; Korean `열린 상태로 실패` does not say what happens when the check itself breaks.
column8: `오류가 나도 막지 않고 통과시킨다`, `오류가 나면 차단한다`

column7: `load-bearing` rendered as the structural-engineering phrase; outside construction Korean `하중` never means 'the thing everything depends on'.
Calque of "it is possible/important to X"; Korean has a direct verb.
Filler discourse markers and inflation adjectives a human writing operations prose does not reach for.
column8: Delete the marker; replace the adjective with the concrete claim

column6: 속도가 아니라 안정성이고 비용이 아니라 시간이다
column7: The generator's favourite contrast frame; one is rhetoric, two in a paragraph is a tic.
column8: State the positive directly; keep at most one per section

column7: `되다` is already passive; `~어지다` doubles it.
A structural metaphor standing in for a noun the writer did not name.
Casual anthropomorphism in otherwise formal prose; mixed register.
Double abstraction: both halves nominalize the same action.

column6: 장애에 대한 대응과 원인에 대한 분석
column7: English "about/regarding"; one is fine, two in a paragraph is stilted.
Abstract object plus a weak verb doubles the awkwardness.
English "X via Z" rendered as a noun modifier.

column6: 장애로 인한 지연에 따른 재시도로 인한 부하
column7: Three causal markers in one paragraph read bureaucratic.
`無X` reads as a stiff back-translation of "zero-/no-X"; the established terms `무중단` and `무손실` are not flagged.
`친숙` is emotional intimacy; tool proficiency wants `익숙`, and an environment does not befriend anything.
`교정` is proofreading or orthopedics and `산재` is formal "dispersed"; both read stiff for a fix or "scattered".
A `로` particle plus an English verb conjugated directly; often paired with a duplicated `로`.
column8: Give the verb a proper Korean target: `클러스터에 join하고`

column7: What shrank was the time, not the delivery itself; the EN half usually still has the unit.
Korean attaches a particle to the preceding word with no space, including after an English word, a closing parenthesis or a percent sign.
column9: DNS는 내부에서|bash/zsh 이식성 검토|re-exec 가드를 강력히 권장|agent 이름에 정의된|plan 가치의 일부|context reset 이후에도 복잡한

column7: A particle after closing markup still attaches with no space.
column9: make test를 실행|`echo` 이상의 일을 하는|따른다.** 이 문서가 다루는 것은|**전부** 이 문제를 만난다

column7: Bare `첫 + noun` reads clipped for "the first run".
'Blocked at the source' is an absolute claim that almost always overstates what one mechanism does.
column8: Name the path actually closed: `~ 경로를 없앰`, `사전에 제거`, `노출면을 줄임`

column7: A risk is a likelihood, not an object; it cannot be blocked or removed - name the path or exposure that was closed.
`로의` stacks a directional particle on the genitive, a construction Korean expresses with a verb; `앞으로의` is not flagged.
column9: 앞으로의 계획|두 워크플로의 자기 재검 단계

column7: 'There was a (structural) limitation' wraps a plain failure in an abstract noun instead of saying what could not be done.
column8: Say what failed with a verb: `추적하기 어려웠습니다`, `~해서 503 에러가 발생했습니다`

column7: `부재` (absence) as a predicate or cause noun is stiff Sino-Korean for 'did not exist'.
A `미-` prefix noun compresses a negated verb into note-taking shorthand; a table cell or checklist is a false positive.
column8: `감지하지 못한 장애`, `일부러 부여하지 않아`, `스케일아웃이 일어나지 않음`

column7: Ending a sentence or clause on the noun `불가` leaves a note fragment where prose needs a predicate; terse notes are a false positive.
'Secured X-ness' names a quality instead of the concrete effect; repeated through a document it reads as generated.
column8: Say what changed: `로그 중복·누락 방지`, `값이 실제와 어긋나지 않게 함`

column7: `X을 활용한` is a padded instrumental where `로` already carries the meaning; a non-tool object (`시간을 활용해`) is natural.
`X을 수행하다` turns the real verb into the object of a dummy 'perform' verb.
`X을 진행하다` is filler that delays the real verb (the particle form of `nominal-progress`).
`X 기반의 Y` stacked as an adnominal calques 'X-based Y' and usually hides a simpler instrumental.
An English gloss after a plain Korean word adds noise; keep a gloss only on the first mention of a genuinely unfamiliar term (see 용어 도입 관례).
column8: Drop the gloss: `환경 불일치`, `영향 범위`, `허용 목록`

column7: An untranslated English idiom inside Korean prose where a plain Korean phrase exists.
column8: `근본 원인`, `단일 기준`, `사람이 직접 확인`, `용량이 큰 이미지`, `배포 시간`

column7: `단일 뷰/체계` is word-for-word 'single view/system'; Korean says 'one screen' or 'one'.
`다중 X` for 'multiple X' is a technical-translation calque; plain Korean uses `여러`. A game-term `다중 인스턴스` is a false positive.
In Korean copy the tilde marks a range (`9~14초`); as an 'approximately' prefix it is an English habit.
`조용한 실패/유실` is a literal 'silent failure/loss'; Korean describes what the reader could not see.
column8: `아무 표시 없이 사라지는 트레이스`, `에러 없이 멈춘 수집`, `감지되지 않는 장애`

column6: 롤백 불능 상태를 핵심 운영 리스크로 정의.
column7: 'Defined X as the core risk/problem' is consultant framing standing in for the judgment itself.
`~이 이루어지다` (to be carried out) is a translationese passive that hides who did what.
`빈번하게 발생했다` is a literal 'frequently occurred'; one adjective carries it.
A clause-modified `이슈` for a malfunction calques 'an issue where X did not work'; Korean says `문제`.
column8: `작동하지 않던 문제`, `네트워크 카드를 못 잡던 문제`

column7: `공수` (工数, man-hours) is Japanese project-management jargon; plain Korean says work or time.
column8: `수동 갱신 작업을 절반으로 줄임`, `연간 약 50시간 절감`

column7: `제로화` is a coined 'zero-ization'; a count reads cleaner.
`net effect` rendered as the economics term `순효과`; in technical prose, name what actually changed.
'Successfully' adds nothing to a completed action and is a common generated-text tell.
column8: Delete it and state the result: `무중단으로 이전했습니다`, `5개 고객사에 납품`

column7: An unquantified intensifier where a number, or nothing, is stronger.
`현대화` is a vague headline noun that says nothing about what changed.
column8: State the change: `ELK → EFK 전환`, `3단계 고도화`

column7: 'Virtuous cycle' is a buzzword that inflates a single causal step.
`체계적인` asserts rigor instead of showing it.
column8: Delete it and describe the structure: `4단계 버전 관리`

column7: `본연의` is ornamental filler.
'Realized X' is an inflated verb for an ordinary result.
column8: `관리 체계를 갖췄습니다`, or the concrete result

column7: `~함과 동시에` is a literal 'at the same time as' that a plain `~고` handles.
'To solve this, …' is a scaffold transition; the causal link is already clear.
column8: Join to the previous sentence: `~를 도출하고`, `그래서`

column7: `~에 직면하다` is a literal 'faced with' that dramatizes an ordinary blocker.
'A limitation existed' translates 'there existed'; Korean uses `있다` or a verb for the failure.
`~에게 있어(서)` is 'for/to someone' translationese, the variant `e-isseoseo` misses.
`~하는 중에 있다` is a literal progressive.
`~에 다름 아니다` is a Japanese-derived 'is nothing other than'.
`X라고 하는 것은` is a wordy topic frame for 'what is called X'.
`~에 위치한` is 'located in' translationese.
The `~하는 데 있어(서)` / `~함에 있어` variants of `에 있어서` (Japanese ~において) that `e-isseoseo` does not reach.
`~로 하여금 ~하게 하다` is a literal causative frame from English 'make/let X do'.
column8: Make the person the subject: `운영자가 판단한다`

column7: 'Makes X possible' rendered literally; Korean puts the ability on the actor.

English third-person pronouns carried over into expository prose; Korean omits them or names who is meant. Narrative prose about people (history, biography) uses `그들` naturally, and `당신` is left out because it opens persona prompts by design.
column8: Drop the pronoun, or name them: `메인테이너의 응답`

column6: 가장 많이 쓰는 도구 중 하나
column7: Calque of 'one of the most X'; Korean rarely hedges a superlative this way.
`~로부터의` stacks a source particle on the genitive, from English 'from X'.
`~에 의한` is English 'by / caused by' as a noun modifier, the adnominal twin of `passive-by`.
`~에도 불구하고` is a stiff 'despite'; the particle `~에도` or `~지만` already carries it.
'Requires X' rendered literally.
'X is required' as a passive of `요구하다`; Korean states the need directly.
'It is recommended / consider doing X' wraps the verb in `것을`.
column8: `최신 버전을 쓰길 권장한다`, `최신 버전을 쓰세요`, `~할지 검토`

column7: 'So-called / called X' rendered literally.
'The number / amount of X' with a genitive; Korean compounds the noun. Natural once, a translation habit when repeated. `경우의 수` is an idiom and is not flagged.
'Has a feature / option' with a concrete noun, which `gajida-abstract` does not cover.
`~하도록 하겠습니다` wraps the verb in an extra causative.
`~에서의` stacks a locative on the genitive; one is fine, a document full of them reads translated.
'This means X' used as a connective; Korean says what follows directly. A definition (`SLO는 ~를 의미한다`) is a false positive.
English plural carried over; Korean leaves an inanimate plural implicit.
'Tends to' rendered literally, and often a hedge.
'Focus on' rendered literally.
`상기 / 하기` (above / below) is Japanese office jargon.
`상이하다` is stiff Sino-Korean for 'different'.
`~할 시` is an administrative clipping of `~할 때`; a noun before `시` (`분할 시`, `배포 시`) is a terse label and not flagged.
column9: 멀티 커밋 분할 시 번호를 매긴다

column7: `제고 / 도모 / 만전을 기하다` are bureaucratic Sino-Korean verbs.
`~을 요하다` is a Japanese-era formal 'requires'.
`사료되다` and `~하는 바이다` are official-document formulas that stiffen technical prose.
`용이하다` is stiff Sino-Korean for 'easy'; repeated it reads like a proposal document.
'Plays an important role' is a generated-text staple that says nothing about what the thing does.
column8: State what it does: `요청을 먼저 검증한다`

column7: 'It can be said that X' hedges a claim the writer could simply make.
`필요성이 대두되다` is a news-report cliche for 'became necessary'.
A passive hedge ('it is judged that') for a judgement the writer made.
Sentence-opening `이는` ('This …') is the generator's favourite link; repeated through a document it reads machine-written.
column8: Join to the previous sentence, or `그래서`, `이 때문에`

column7: Marketing adjectives ('powerful', 'seamlessly', 'smoothly') that assert quality instead of showing it.
column8: Delete, or state the concrete property

column7: `다양한` is the generator's default quantifier; a document full of it never says which.
'Not only X but also Y' used as a sentence template; repeated through a document it reads generated.
Blog-template signposting ('let us look at'); repeated per section it reads machine-written.
'Helps with X' is a vague benefit claim; repeated it replaces saying what improved.
column8: State the effect: `장애 원인을 바로 찾는다`

column7: `이러한` is a formal demonstrative a generator repeats; everyday prose uses `이런` or `이`.
The Korean punctuation rules (문장 부호, 2015) put no comma after a common sentence-opening connective such as `그러나` or `따라서`; the comma is an English habit.
A note-style ending (`함`, `됨`, `임`) fused with `다`, a slip between the note style and the plain style.
`되어` contracts to `돼`: `됐다`, `돼요`, `돼서`, `안 돼요`.
column9: 로그는 공개하지 않되 기록은 남긴다|적용돼서 다행이다

column7: A common misspelling; Markdown editors rarely run a spell-checker.
`수` is a bound noun and takes a space: `할 수 있다`.
`것` is a bound noun and takes a space before `같다`.
The negative adverb `안` is written apart from `되다`; joined, `안되다` means 'pitiable'.
`아니에요` and `거예요` are the standard forms, and `-읍니다` after `있`, `없`, `했` was replaced by `-습니다` in 1988. `모읍니다` (from `모으다`) is correct and not flagged.
column9: 모든 항목을 한 곳에 모읍니다|두 시각의 차이였습니다|두 값 사이예요

column7: The future / conjecture ending is `겠`, not `겟`.
`않` is the contraction of `아니하` and follows `~지`; `안` is the adverb before a verb. They are swapped here.
`로서` marks a capacity or status (`개발자로서`); `로써` marks a means (`대화로써`).
Free choice ('whatever, wherever') is `든(지)`; `던` marks the past.
A misplaced or missing 사이시옷: Sino-Korean compounds such as `개수`, `대가`, `초점` take none, and `위층`, `뒤풀이`, `해님` drop it before an aspirated consonant; `장밋빛`, `등굣길` need one.
`때` is a noun and is written apart from the modifier before it.
`것` is a bound noun and takes a space after its modifier.
`밖에` is a particle and attaches: `수밖에 없다`.
`지` meaning 'since' is a bound noun and takes a space.
The verb after a particle (`대한`, `통해`, `위한`, …) is its own word and takes a space.
The negative adverb `안` is written apart from `하다`.
Korean attaches `%` to its number.
A space before a period, comma or question mark.
A native word repeats the meaning of the Sino-Korean prefix after it (`다시` = `재-`, `미리` = `예-`, `가장` = `최-`).
`약` already means approximately; `정도`, `가량`, `여` say it again.
`매-` and `마다` both mean 'every'.
`에게` is for people and animals; an organisation or a thing takes `에`.
`X들 중의 하나` renders 'one of the Xs' word for word, plural and genitive included.
The quantifier already makes a thing plural; `들` repeats it, an English habit. Nouns for people (`사용자`, `이주민`) are not flagged.
`-시키다` on a verb whose `-하다` form already takes the object; dictionary causatives such as `향상시키다` or `종료시키다` are not flagged.
A passive stem (`잊히다`, `짜이다`, `닫히다`) that takes `-어지다` again, beyond the forms `ai-double-passive` covers.
'Held a meeting' rendered as `갖다`, a translation habit.

column6: 쉽게 배포할 수 있도록 해 준다
column7: 'Allows / enables X to' rendered literally; Korean states what X can now do.
`보다` as a free-standing adverb calques English 'more'; Korean says `더`.

column6: 보안에 관한 규칙과 배포에 관한 절차
column7: `에 관한` is the twin of `에 대한`; two in one paragraph read stilted.

column6: 배포를 위한 설정을 위한 도구를 위한 문서
column7: Three `~을 위한` modifiers in one paragraph stack English 'for'.
`의거하다` is legal-document register.
`~고 있다` and `중` both mark progress.
Two hedges stacked on one claim (`수 있다` + `것 같다`).
column8: `해결할 수 있습니다`, or state the doubt once

column7: 'Beyond a mere X' is a generated-text inflation frame.
A signpost ('what is notable is') that delays the point; repeated it reads generated.
Presentation buzzwords that stand in for a concrete claim.
column8: Name the change: `새 팀으로 옮겼다`, `비용을 절반으로 줄였다`

column7: `시사하는 바가 크다` is an editorial cliche that never names the lesson; a `시사점` heading in a research note is fine.
`~하고자 합니다` repeated through a document is stiff, speech-like signposting.
`~하는 부분` as a verbal filler, a spoken habit carried into writing.
`~것 같습니다` repeated through a document hedges every claim.
column8: Assert what you know; hedge only where you are unsure

column7: 'There exists X' rendered with `존재하다`; Korean says `있다`.
'Such as' rendered as `~와 같은`; a document full of it reads translated. `다음과 같은` / `아래와 같은` introduce a list and are not flagged; `X와 같은 Y` meaning 'the same Y as X' is a false positive.
Two `~적인` modifiers in a row stack Sino-Korean adjectives.
column8: Keep one, or use a verb: `효율적으로 짜인 관리`

column7: A loanword spelled against the loanword orthography (외래어 표기법). Only spellings whose standard form dominates real Korean technical writing are listed; `타겟`, `디렉토리`, `컨셉` and `뱃지` are left out because common usage has not settled on the standard form.
`율` follows a vowel or `ㄴ` (`참여율`, `전환율`); `률` follows any other final consonant (`이탈률`, `사용률`).
The bound noun is `거` (from `것`); `꺼` is a spoken spelling, and it takes a space after the modifier.
`돼` is the contraction of `되어`; where no `어` belongs (`되는`, `되고`, `되면`, `된`) the stem stays `되`.
The ending is `-ㄹ는지`; `-ㄹ런지` is a spoken spelling.
These `-하다` stems form their adverb with `-히` (`정확히`, `충분히`); `-이` belongs to stems such as `깨끗이` and `일일이`.
A misspelt verb or word: an adjective that takes `-은` (`걸맞은`), a stem with a spurious `이` or `하` (`설레다`, `삼가다`), a wrong contraction (`치렀다`, `잠갔다`, `바뀌었다`), or a word such as `가리키다`, `헷갈리다`, `귀띔`.
column9: 상황에 걸맞은 설정|포인터가 가리키는 값|더 나은 방법

column7: `만큼`, `대로`, `뿐`, `줄` and `채` after a verb modifier are bound nouns and take a space; after a plain noun (`규칙대로`, `이것뿐`) they are particles and attach.
column8: `원하는 대로`, `할 만큼`, `할 뿐`, `할 줄 안다`, `켠 채로`

column7: `시` (when), `간` (between) and `내` (within) after a noun are bound nouns and take a space; dictionary compounds such as `비상시` and `평상시` are not flagged.
column9: 배포 시 로그를 확인한다|노드 간 통신|비상시에는|사용시간|종료시킨다

column7: A particle is part of the word before it; `부터` after `로` / `에서`, and a stray `을` / `를`, attach with no space.

column6: 다음 명령으로 설정 할 수 있다
column7: `하다` / `되다` after a Sino-Korean noun is a suffix and attaches (`설정할`, `사용되는`).
column9: 다음 명령으로 설정할 수 있다|설정 한 번으로 끝난다|요청 하나를 보낸다

column7: 'As soon / many as possible' is `가능한 한 ~`; `가능한` alone is an adjective ('a possible X') and cannot carry the adverb.
column9: 가능한 한 빨리 배포한다|가능한 방법을 찾는다

column7: `~하지 않으면 안 된다` is the Japanese `~なければならない` frame; Korean states the obligation. A literal 'if you do not X, it will not work' is a false positive.
`~에 의하면` is the Japanese `~によれば`; Korean cites a source with `~에 따르면`.
`~을 행하다` is a formal dummy verb for the action the noun already names.
`~에 기인하다` is written-register Sino-Korean for a plain cause.
